<meta>This page continues the catalog of pagan deities and their origins as described by Isidore of Seville. Having previously discussed Janus and Jupiter, the text now focuses on the "Great Mother" (the Earth), Vesta, Juno, Minerva, Venus, and other deities, explaining their symbols and names through historical and allegorical lenses.</meta>

# VIII

<column-break/>

whether she is clothed in various things or stands by her own strength <note>A wordplay on "Vesta" and "vis," meaning strength.</note>. They also imagine her to be both the Earth and the **Great Mother**: crowned with towers, accompanied by a drum, a rooster, and the clash of cymbals. She is called "Mother" because she gives birth to so many things; "Great" because she produces food; and "Nurturing" <note>original: "alma"</note> because she feeds all animals with her fruits. For the earth is the nurse of all sustenance. Her image is portrayed with a **key**, because the earth is locked <note>original: "clauditur"</note> in winter and opened <note>original: "apitur"</note> in spring so that crops may grow. She has a **drum**, by which they wish to signify the orb of the earth. She is said to be carried in a **chariot** because the earth itself hangs in the air. It is supported by **wheels** because the world is rotating and revolving. They place tame **lions** under her to show that no species on earth is so wild that it cannot be subdued or overcome by her. On her head, she wears a **turreted crown** to show that cities situated upon the earth are distinguished by their towers. They imagine **seats** around her because, while all things move, she herself does not move. Her ministers, the **Corybantes**, are depicted with drawn swords to signify that everyone ought to fight for their land. They gave her **roosters** <note>original: "Gallos," referring to the priests of Cybele</note> to serve her, signifying that those who lack "seed" <note>A reference to the ritual castration of these priests</note> ought to follow the earth, for in her, all things are found. They throw themselves down before her and command, they say, that those who cultivate the earth should not sit idle, for there is always something to do. The sound of the **bronze cymbals** represents the clattering of iron tools in the cultivation of fields; and they are made of bronze because the ancients cultivated the earth with bronze before iron was discovered. They claim **Vesta** and **fire** are the same thing, for there is no doubt that the earth possesses fire, as can be understood from Mount Etna and the fires of Vulcan. And for this reason, they think she is a **virgin**, because fire is an inviolable element, and nothing can be born from it; indeed, it consumes everything it seizes. As **Ovid** says in the *Fasti*: "Think of Vesta as nothing other than a living flame. You see that no bodies are born from flame." For this reason, they say virgins serve her, because just as nothing is born from a virgin, so nothing is born from fire. They call **Juno** as if from "Janona," that is, a "doorway" <note>original: "ianua"</note>, because of the purifications of women, and because she opens, as it were, the gates for matrons and the nature of brides for their husbands. This is what the philosophers say. The learned, however, assert that Juno is the sister and wife of **Jove**. For they interpret Jove as fire and air, and Juno as water and earth. From the mixing of these two, all things are born. She is called his "sister" because she is part of the same world-system, and his "wife" because she is joined and united with him. Hence **Virgil** says: "Then the Almighty Father, the Sky <note>original: "Ether"</note>, descends with fertile rains into the lap of his joyful wife." **Minerva** is called **Athena** by the Greeks, which means "woman." Among the Latins, she is called Minerva as if she were a goddess <note>original: "deam"</note> and the gift of various arts. For they claim she is the inventor of many talents, and thus they interpret her as "art" and "reason," because without reason nothing can be maintained. Since this reason is born from the mind alone—and they believe the mind is in the head and brain—they say she was born from the **head of Jove**, because the sense of the wise man, which discovers all things, is in the head. Therefore, the **head of a Gorgon** is depicted on her breast, because there lies all the prudence that confounds others, or proves them to be unskilled and foolish; just as we see in the ancient statues of commanders, placed in the middle of the

<column-break/>

breastplate <note>original: "lorica"</note> to suggest wisdom and courage. This Minerva is also called **Tritonia**. For Triton is a marsh in Africa around which they say she appeared in the form of a young girl, for which reason she was named Tritonia. Hence she was believed to be a goddess all the more readily because her origin was less known. She is called **Pallas** either from the island of Pallene in Thrace where she was raised, or from the Greek "to brandish the spear" <note>original Greek: "pallein to dory"</note>, or because she killed the giant Pallas. They say **Venus** was named from the fact that a woman does not cease to be a virgin without "force" <note>original: "vi"</note>. The Greeks call her **Aphrodite** because of the foam of blood that generates life. For in Greek, "foam" is called *aphros*. They imagine that **Saturn** cut off the genitals of his father **Caelus** <note>The Sky</note> and the blood flowed into the sea; and from that thickened sea-foam, Venus was born. They say this because the substance of sexual intercourse is a foamy moisture, and thus Venus is called Aphrodite because intercourse is the foam of blood, which consists of the liquid and foamy moisture of the internal organs. They say Venus is the wife of **Vulcan** because the office of Venus does not exist without heat; hence the saying: "The old man is cold toward Venus." For the story that Saturn cut off his father Caelus's virility, which fell into the sea and created Venus, is imagined for this reason: unless moisture descends from the sky to the earth, nothing is created. They say **Cupid** is named after "love" <note>original: "amorem"</note>. For he is the demon of fornication. He is depicted with **wings** because nothing is found to be lighter or more changeable than lovers. He is painted as a **boy** because love is foolish and irrational. He is imagined to hold an **arrow** and a **torch**: the arrow because love wounds the heart, the torch because it inflames it. The Greeks speak of **Pan**, whom the Latins call **Silvanus**, the god of rustics, whom they formed in the likeness of nature. Hence he is called Pan, which means "All" <note>original: "omne"</note>. For they imagine him from the universal appearance of the elements. He has **horns** in the likeness of the rays of the sun and moon. He has a **spotted skin** because of the stars in the sky. His **face is red**, like the upper air <note>original: "etheris"</note>. He carries a **flute of seven reeds** because of the harmony of heaven, in which there are seven sounds and seven intervals of voices. He is **hairy** because the earth is covered [with plants] and stirred by winds. His **lower part is foul** because of the trees, wild beasts, and cattle. He has **goat hooves** to show the solidity of the earth. They wish him to be the god of all things and of nature itself, hence "Pan" is said to be as if "all things." **Isis** in the language of the Egyptians is the name for the Earth, which they want Isis to be. For Isis was a queen of the Egyptians, daughter of King Inachus, who came from Greece and taught the Egyptians letters and how to cultivate the land; for this reason, they called the earth by her name. **Serapis** is the greatest god of all the Egyptians. He is actually **Apis**, king of the Argives, who was carried by ship to Egypt, and having died there, was called Serapis. This is because the chest in which a dead person is placed, which they call a **sarcophagus**, is called *soros* in Greek; and they began to worship him there as one buried before his temple was built, like a "soros." Thus he was first "Apis-sorapis," then by changing one letter, he was called Serapis. Among the Egyptians, **Apis** was a bull consecrated to Serapis and named after him, whom the Egyptians worshipped like a deity because of future events...

<summary>This page explores the symbolic meanings and etymologies of various Greco-Roman and Egyptian gods, interpreting their physical attributes—such as Minerva's Gorgon breastplate and Pan's goat legs—as allegories for natural phenomena and human qualities.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the catalog of pagan supernatural beings and concepts, moving from the "Great Mother" to Fate, spirits of the home and wild, and finally transitioning into Book IX, which discusses the origin of human languages at the Tower of Babel.</meta>

...gave certain manifest signs. For he appeared in Memphis <note>referring to the sacred bull Apis</note>. A hundred priests followed him, suddenly singing out as if they were possessed <term>lymphatici: those driven mad by water nymphs</term>. They made an image of a head appear to themselves in the desert. **Fauns** are named from "speaking" <note>Latin: "fando"</note>, as if from "the voice" <note>original Greek: "apo tēs phōnēs"</note>, because they seemed to show the future by voice rather than by signs. For they were consulted in groves by pagans, and gave responses to them not by signs but by voices. They say a **Genius** is so named because it has the power of "begetting" <note>Latin: "gignendarum"</note> all things, or from begetting children. From this, "genial beds" were also named by the nations, which were prepared for a new husband. These and others are the fabulous fictions of the heathens, which are interpreted in such a way that, while not understood, they are damnabily worshiped. However, they say **Fate** <note>Latin: "Fatum"</note> is whatever the gods speak <note>Latin: "fantur"</note>, or whatever Jupiter speaks. Therefore, from "speaking" <note>Latin: "fando"</note> it is called "fate," that is, from talking. If this name were not already commonly understood to mean something else <note>Isidore is wary of the pagan concept of deterministic fate</note>, we could rationally call it "fate" from "speaking," for we cannot deny that it is written in the Holy Scriptures: "God has spoken once; these two things have I heard," and so on. For what was said "once" is understood as "immovably"—that is, He has spoken unchangeably, just as He knows unchangeably all things that will be and what He Himself will do. 

They imagine three **Fates** with a distaff, a spindle, and fingers twisting threads from wool, representing the three divisions of time. The **past** is what is already spun and wound onto the spindle; the **present** is what is being passed between the fingers of the spinner; and the **future** is the wool wrapped on the distaff, which is still to be passed through the fingers of the spinner to the spindle, just as the present must pass into the past. They say the **Parcae** <note>the Roman Fates</note> are named "by antiphrasis" <term>antiphrasis: naming something by its opposite quality</term> because they "spare" <note>Latin: "parcant"</note> no one. They wished for there to be three: one who begins a man’s life, a second who weaves it, and a third who breaks it. For we begin when we are born, we exist while we live, and we cease when we die. They say **Fortune** takes her name from "fortuitous" events, as if she were a goddess mocking human affairs with various and accidental chances. Whence they also call her blind, because she runs into anyone here and there without any examination of merit, coming to both the good and the bad. 

They separate **Fate** from **Fortune**: Fortune is as if in those things which come by chance with no obvious cause, while they say **Fate** is assigned and established for each individual. They also say there are three **Furies**, women with hair made of snakes, representing the three effects that generate many perturbations in the minds of men and sometimes compel them to sin so that they permit no respect for their own reputation or danger: **Anger**, which desires vengeance; **Greed**, which desires wealth; and **Lust**, which appetites pleasures. These are called "Furies" because they strike the mind with their stings and do not allow it to be at rest. They believe **Nymphs** are goddesses of the waters, named from "clouds" <note>Latin: "nubibus"</note>. For water comes from clouds, from which the name is derived; they also call nymphs "waters" and "**Muses**," and not without reason, for the movement of water produces music. Among the heathens, there are various names for Nymphs: they call those of the mountains **Oreads**, those of the forests **Dryads**, those of the springs **Hamadryads**, those of the fields **Naiads**, and those of the sea **Nereids**. They say the name **Heroes** passed over from Juno—for in Greek, Juno is called 

<column-break/>

**Hera**. And therefore, some son of hers, according to the Greek fable, was called a **Hero**. This is a mystical fable, signifying that the air <note>Latin: "aer"</note> is assigned to Juno, where they want the heroes to inhabit. By this name they call the souls of the deceased who possess some merit, as if they were "heroes"—that is, men of the air and worthy of heaven because of their wisdom and fortitude. 

The heathens called all the gods they worshiped at home **Penates**. They were called "Penates" because they were in the "innermost parts" <note>Latin: "penetrabilibus"</note>, that is, in secret places. Where they were called gods, or what names they had, is unknown. They say the **Manes** are the gods of the dead, whose power they assert is between the moon and the earth; they are thought to be named from "the morning" <note>Latin: "mane"</note> because they are thought to be "thin" <note>Latin: "manum"</note>, that is, rare. They are called **Manes** either because they "flow widely" <note>Latin: "manant"</note> through the breezes, or because they are mild <note>Latin: "mites"</note>, being called so by the opposite name to "monstrous" <note>Latin: "imanes"</note>. But Apuleius says they are called Manes by antiphrasis: that is, they are called mild and modest when they are actually terrible and monstrous, like the Parcae or the Eumenides. They say **Larvae** are demons made from men who were of evil merit. Their nature is said to be to terrify children and to chatter in dark corners. **Lamiae**, which fables say used to snatch and tear infants, are specifically named from "tearing" <note>Latin: "laniando"</note>. The "Hairy Ones," who in Greek are called **Panites** and in Latin **Incubi**, are also called **Inui** from "entering" <note>Latin: "ineundo"</note> everywhere with animals. Whence they are also called "Incubi" from "lying upon" <note>Latin: "incubando"</note>, that is, committing illicit acts. For often these wicked spirits also accost women and perform intercourse with them; the Gauls call these demons **Dusii**, because they constantly perform this uncleanness. He whom the common people call an "Incubo," the Romans call **Faunus Ficarius**, to whom Horace says: "Faunus, lover of fleeing nymphs, pass gently through my borders and sunny fields." Others call this being a **Satyr**.

->Here begins the ninth book<-
->On the languages of nations, Chapter I<-

Diversity of languages arose during the building of the tower after the flood. For before that proud tower divided human society into various sounds of signs, there was one language for all nations, which is called **Hebrew**: which the patriarchs and prophets used not only in their speech but also in the sacred letters. In the beginning, there were as many languages as there were nations. Then, there were more nations than languages, because many nations arose from one language. "Languages" are so called in this place for the "words" which are made through the tongue, using that figure of speech where the thing that acts is named by the instrument that performs the action—just as the "mouth" is often said for "words," or the "hand" for "writing." 

There are, however, three sacred languages: **Hebrew**, **Greek**, and **Latin**, which excel most in all the world. For in these three languages, the cause of the Lord <note>the "titulus" or inscription on the Cross</note> was written by Pilate. Therefore, because of the obscurity of the Holy Scriptures, knowledge of these three languages is necessary, so that one may have recourse to another if any doubt about a word...

<meta>This page continues Book IX of the Etymologies, moving from the philosophical origins of speech to a linguistic and genealogical survey of the world’s peoples. ### On Languages and Nations

...or what the speech of one language has brought forth in interpretation. Among all other nations, the **Greek** language is held to be the most famous. It is more resonant than Latin or any other tongue. Its variety is distinguished into five parts. Of these, the first is called <note>original: "cenedo," a corruption of "Koine"</note> **Common**, which everyone uses. The second is **Attic**, namely that of the Athenians, which all the Greek authors used. The third is **Doric**, which the Egyptians and Syrians possess. The fourth is **Ionic**. The fifth is **Aeolic**, which the Aeolians were said to speak. There are certain distinct differences of this kind in the observation of the Greek tongue, for the "Common" speech is divided in this way.

Some have said there are four **Latin** languages: that is, the **Ancient**, the **Latin**, the **Roman**, and the **Mixed**. The *Ancient* is the unrefined tongue used by the oldest people of Italy under Janus and Saturn, such as are found in the songs of the Salii <note>The Salii were "leaping priests" of Mars who sang archaic, nearly unintelligible hymns</note>. The *Latin* was spoken by others in Latium under King Latinus and the Tuscan kings; from this, the Twelve Tables were written. The *Roman* began after the kings were driven out by the Roman people; this is what the poets Naevius, Plautus, Ennius, and Virgil, and the orators Gracchus, Cato, Cicero, and others poured forth. The *Mixed* language broke into the Roman state after the empire was further extended, along with new customs and people, corrupting the integrity of speech through <term>solecisms: grammatical errors</term> and <term>barbarisms: use of non-standard or foreign words</term>.

All the nations of the East clash their tongue and words in the throat, like the Hebrews and Syrians. All Mediterranean nations strike their speech against the palate, like the Greeks and Asians. All Western nations break their words against the teeth, like the Italians and Spaniards. The **Syriac** and **Chaldean** tongues are close to Hebrew, harmonizing in many sounds and letters. Some, however, think that the first language was Chaldean, because Abraham was from the Chaldeans. If this is accepted, how is it that in the book of Daniel the Hebrew youths are ordered to be taught a language they did not know? 

Every person can grasp any language—whether Greek, Latin, or those of other nations—either by hearing it, by reading it, or by receiving it from a teacher. Since the knowledge of all languages is difficult for anyone, no one is so lazy that, being placed among his own people, he does not know the language of his own nation. For what else should such a person be thought, if not worse than brute animals? For they express the cry of their own voice, but he is worse who lacks the knowledge of his own tongue.

It is difficult to find what kind of language **God** spoke at the beginning of the world when He said, "Let there be light." For there were not yet any languages. Likewise, in what language His voice later sounded to the outer ears of men, especially when speaking to the first man, or to the prophets, or when the voice of God speaking sounded physically: "You are my beloved son." In these cases, it is believed by some that He used that one and only language which existed before there was a diversity of tongues. However, among various nations, it is believed that God speaks to them in the same language that the people themselves use, so that He may be understood by them. God speaks to men not through an invisible substance, but through a physical creature, through which He also wished to appear to men when He spoke. The Apostle also says: "If I speak with the tongues of men and of angels..."

<column-break/>

...where it is asked: in what language do **angels** speak? It is not that angels have actual languages, but this is said for the sake of <term>exaggeration: hyperbole</term>. Likewise, it is asked in what language men will speak in the future, but this is nowhere found. For the Apostle says: "Whether tongues, they shall cease." Therefore, we have placed the discussion of languages before that of nations, because nations arose from languages, not languages from nations.

->**Chapter II: On the Names of Nations**<-

A **Nation** <note>original: "Gens"</note> is a multitude of people arising from one origin, or distinguished from another nation according to its own proper grouping, such as the different peoples of Greece. From this comes the word "gentility." A nation is so called because of the "generations" of families—that is, from "begetting" <note>Latin: "gignendo"</note>, just as a "race" <note>Latin: "natio"</note> comes from "being born" <note>Latin: "nascendo"</note>.

There are **seventy-two** nations from which the earth was divided. From **Japheth** come fifteen plus one; from **Ham**, thirty; from **Shem**, twenty-seven; which make seventy-two. Or rather, as reason declares, seventy-two languages began to exist throughout the lands, and as they grew, they filled the provinces and islands.

The five sons of **Shem** individually produced single nations. The first was **Elam**, from whom came the Elamites, the princes of Persia. The second was **Assur**, from whom the empire of the Assyrians sprouted. The third was **Arphaxad**, from whom the nation of the Chaldeans arose. The fourth was **Lud**, from whom came the Lydians. The fifth was **Aram**, from whom the Syrians came, whose metropolis was Damascus.

The four sons of Aram, grandsons of Shem: **Uz**, **Hul**, **Gether**, and **Mash**. Uz was the founder of Trachonitis, who held power between Palestine and Coele-Syria, from where Job came, according to what is written: "There was a man in the land of Uz named Job." The second was Hul, from whom the Armenians came. The third was Gether, from whom the Carmanians or Carians came. The fourth was Mash, from whom are those who are called Meonians. 

The posterity of Arphaxad son of Shem: **Eber** was the grandson of Arphaxad, from whom are the Hebrews. **Joktan** was the son of Eber, from whom the nation of the Indians arose. **Shelah** was the son of Joktan, from whom the Bactrians came, though others suspect them to be exiles of the Scythians. **Ishmael** was the son of Abraham, from whom are the Ishmaelites, who are now called by the corrupted name **Saracens** (as if from Sarah) and **Hagarenes** (from Hagar). **Nebaioth** was the son of Ishmael, from whom are the Nabateans, who live from Euphrata to the Red Sea. **Moab** and **Ammon** were the sons of Lot, from whom came the Moabites and Ammonites. **Edom** was the son of Esau, from whom are the Idumeans. These are the nations that descend from the stock of Shem, possessing the southern land from the rising of the sun as far as Phoenicia.

The four sons of **Ham**, from whom these nations arose: **Cush**, from whom the Ethiopians were begotten. **Mizraim**, from whom the Egyptians arose. **Phut**, from whom the Libyans came. From this, the river of Mauretania is called "Phut" even to the present, and all the region around it is "Phutensis." **Canaan**, from whom the Africans, Phoenicians, and the ten nations of the Canaanites came.

Likewise, from the grandsons of Ham: the sons of Cush, the grandson of Ham, were six. The sons of Cush were Seba, Havilah, Sabtah, Raamah, Sabtecha, and Cush <note>text varies slightly from Genesis</note>. From **Seba** were begotten and named the Sabeans, of whom Virgil said: "The incense-bearing branch is for the Sabeans alone." These are also the Arabians. From **Havilah** came the Getulians in the remote part of Africa. From **Sabtah** came the Sabateni, who are now called Astabari. Raamah and Sabtecha gradually lost their ancient names, and it is ignored what they are now called by the ancients. The sons of Raamah were **Sheba** and **Dedan**...

<meta>This page continues the genealogical and linguistic survey of the world’s peoples from Book IX of the Etymologies. ### IX 44

This **Saba**, however, is written with the letter *sin* in Hebrew; the earlier Saba <note>mentioned on a previous page or in a previous section</note> was written with *samech*, from whom the **Sabeans** are named. This Saba is now called **Arabia**. **Dadan** is the ancestor of a nation of **Ethiopia** in the western region. The sons of **Mizraim** <note>original: "Mesraim"; the biblical name for Egypt</note> include **Lehabim**, from whom come the **Libyans**, who were formerly called **Phutites**. From the **Casluhim** <note>original: "Lesloim"</note> came the **Philistines**, whom the ancients called "Allophili" <note>original: "allophilos," meaning "of another race" or "foreigners"</note> and whom we now corruptly call **Palestinians**. Regarding the other six nations of the "Allophili," they are unknown; they were overturned in the Ethiopian war until the memory of their former names perished.

There were eleven sons of **Canaan**, from whom came the ten nations of Canaanites whose land the Jews possessed after being twice expelled. Their firstborn was **Sidon**, from whom the **Sidonians** come; hence their city in Phoenicia is called Sidon. The second was **Heth**, from whom come the **Hethites**. The third was **Jebus**, from whom the **Jebusites** come, who once held **Jerusalem**. The fourth was the **Amorite**, from whom come the **Amorites**. The fifth was the **Girgashite**, from whom come the **Girgashites**. The sixth was the **Hivite**, from whom come the **Hivites**; these are the **Gibeonites** from the city of Gibeon who came as suppliants to Joshua. The seventh was the **Arkite**, who founded the town of **Arka** opposite Tripoli, situated at the roots of Mount Lebanon. The eighth was the **Sinite** <note>original: "asineus"</note>, from whom come the **Sinites**. The ninth was the **Arvadite**, from whom come the **Arvadites**, who occupied the island of **Arvad**, separated from the Phoenician coast by a narrow strait. The tenth was the **Hamathite** <note>original: "amareus"</note>, from whom comes the noble city of **Syria** called **Coeles** <note>likely referring to Coele-Syria or Emesa</note>. The eleventh was the **Amathean**. These are the nations from the line of **Ham**, who hold the entire southern part from Sidon to the **Strait of Gades** <note>The Strait of Gibraltar</note>.

Likewise, there are the tribes of the sons of **Japheth**. Seven sons of Japheth are named: **Gomer**, from whom come the **Galatians**, that is, the **Gauls**. **Magog**, from whom people believe the **Scythians** and **Goths** trace their origin. **Madai**, from whom they think the **Medes** exist. **Javan**, from whom come the **Ionians**, who are also the **Greeks**; hence the **Ionian Sea**. **Tubal**, from whom come the **Iberians**, who are also the **Spanish**, though some suspect the **Italians** come from him as well. **Meshech**, from whom come the **Cappadocians**; hence a city among them is called **Mazaca** <note>original: "malecca"</note> to this day. **Tiras**, from whom come the **Thracians**, whose name is not much changed, as if they were "Tiracians."

The sons of Gomer and grandsons of Japheth are: **Ashkenaz**, from whom come the **Sarmatians**, whom the Greeks call **Reginoi**. **Riphath**, from whom come the **Paphlagonians**. **Togarmah**, from whom are the **Phrygians**. The sons of Javan are **Elishah**, from whom come the Greeks called **Aeolians** <note>original: "colides"</note>; hence the fifth Greek language is called Aeolic. **Tarshish**, from whom come the **Cilicians**, as Josephus believes; hence their metropolis is called **Tarsus**. **Kittim**, from whom come the **Kittim**, that is, the **Cypriots**, from whom the city of **Citium** is named today. **Dodanim**, from whom come the **Rhodians**. These are the nations from the line of Japheth, who possess the middle part of Asia from Mount Taurus to the north, and all of **Europe** as far as the **British Ocean**, leaving their names to places and nations, though many of these were later changed; the rest remain as they were. Indeed, the names of many nations have partly remained, so that today it is clear from where they were derived, such as the **Assyrians** from **Assur**, or the **Hebrews** from **Eber**. Part, however, have been so changed by the passage of time that even the most learned men, searching through the most ancient histories, have not been able to find the origins of all—no, not even some—of these nations. For those Egyptians who arose from the son of Ham called Mizraim, the origin of the name does not resonate in the word "Egyptian," just as it does not for the **Ethiopians**, who are said to belong to that son of Ham called **Cush**.

<column-break/>

And if all things are considered, many names of nations appear changed while others remain; to these, various reasons later gave different names. For the **Indians** were named after the **Indus River**, which encloses them on the western side. The **Seres** <note>The Chinese</note> took their name from their principal town; they are a nation situated in the East, among whom a "wool" <note>Silk</note> is woven from trees. Of them it is said: *The Seres are unknown in face, but known for their fleece.* The **Gangaridae** are those dwelling among the Assyrians and Indians around the **Ganges River**, whence they are called Gangaridae. The **Hyrcanians** are named after the **Hyrcanian forest**, where there are many tigers. The **Bactrians** were Scythians who, driven from their homes by a faction of their own people, settled by the **Bactros**, a river of the East, from whose name they also received their name. The king of this nation was **Zoroaster**, the inventor of the magic art.

The **Parthians** also trace their origin from the Scythians; for they were their exiles, which is also shown by their name. For in the Scythian language, exiles are called "Parthi." These, like the Bactrians, were driven from Scythia by domestic seditions and first secretly occupied the wasteland near **Hyrcania**, and then obtained most of the territories by courage. The **Assyrians** are named after **Assur**, the son of Shem, a most powerful nation that held the entire middle region from the Euphrates to the borders of the Indians. The **Medes** are thought to be named after their king; for **Jason**, the brother of King Pelias, was driven from Thessaly by the sons of Pelias with his wife **Medea**, whose stepson was **Medus**, the king of the Athenians. After the death of Jason, Medus conquered the eastern region, founded the city of **Media** there, and called the nation "Medes" after his own name. But we find in **Genesis** that **Madai** was the founder of the nation of the Medes, from whom they were named as was said above.

The **Persians** were named after King **Perseus**, who, crossing from Greece to Asia, conquered the barbarian nations there in a heavy and long-lasting war. Finally, as victor, he gave his name to the subject nation. Before **Cyrus**, however, the Persians were ignoble and held no place among the nations. The Medes were always the most powerful. The **Chaldeans**, who are now called Chaldeans, were named after **Chesed** <note>original: "caseth"</note>, the son of **Nahor**, the brother of Abraham. The **Sabeans** are named "from the act of worship" <note>original: "ἀπὸ τοῦ σεβεσθαι" [apo tou sebesthai], which means to worship or venerate</note>, because we venerate divinity primarily with frankincense. They are also the **Arabs**, because they are in the mountains of Arabia called **Lebanon** and **Anti-Lebanon**, where frankincense is gathered.

The **Syrians** are said to be named after **Asshurim**, who was a grandson of Abraham by **Keturah**. Those whom the ancients called **Assyrians**, we now call **Syrians**, naming the whole after a part. The **Hebrews** were named after **Eber**, who was a great-grandson of Shem. The **Israelites**, however, were named after **Israel**, the son of Isaac; for it is established that Israel was the patriarch of the Hebrews, from whom the twelve tribes of Israel received their name. For the **Jews**, however, the division of the ten tribes imposed names; for previously they were called Hebrews or Israelites. But since the people of God were divided into two kingdoms, then the two tribes which had kings from the line of **Judah** received the name of **Jews**. The remaining part of the ten tribes, which established a king for itself in **Samaria**, retained the ancient name of **Israel** due to the size of the population.

It explains how geographical features, mythological heroes, and linguistic shifts resulted in the diverse names of nations known in late antiquity.</summary>

<meta>This page continues Isidore of Seville's genealogical history of nations, moving from the immediate descendants of Noah's sons into the origins of the Samaritans, the peoples of the Levant, the Egyptians, and the various tribes of Scythia and Greece.</meta>

# Book IX

<margin>The Samaritans</margin>
The race of the **Samaritans** took its beginning from the Assyrians who migrated and lived in Samaria. In Latin, their name is interpreted as "guards" <note>original: "custodes"</note> because, when Israel was taken captive, these people were stationed to guard the land of that region. **Phoenix**, the brother of Cadmus, set out from Egyptian Thebes into Syria and reigned at Sidon; he called the people **Phoenicians** after his own name, and named the province **Phoenicia**.

<margin>The Sidonians, Saracens, and Ishmaelites</margin>
The **Sidonians**, however, are said to have derived their name from the city called Sidon. The **Saracens** are so named either because they claim to be born from Sarah, or, as the pagans say, because they are of Syrian origin, as if the word were *syrigenae* <note>meaning "Syrian-born"</note>. These people live throughout a vast wilderness. They are the **Ishmaelites**, as the Book of Genesis teaches, because they descend from Ishmael. They are also called **Kedarites** after Cedar, the son of Ishmael; and **Hagarenes** after Hagar. As we have said, they are called **Saracens** by a perversion of the name, because they boast that they are descended from Sarah.

<margin>The Hagarenes, Philistines, and "Allophyli"</margin>
The **Philistines** are the same as the **Palestinians**; the Hebrew language does not have the letter *P*, so they use the Greek *Phi* <note>Φ</note> instead. Thus, they are called Philistines instead of Palestinians, certainly after their own city. They are also called **Allophyli** <note>original: "allophyli," meaning "those of another race"</note>, that is, "foreign-born," because they were always enemies of Israel and were separated far from their lineage and society.

<margin>The Canaanites</margin>
The **Canaanites** are named after Canaan, the son of Ham, whose land the Jews possessed. From his lineage came **Hamor**, the father of Shechem, from whom the **Amorites** were named.

<margin>The Amorites and Egyptians</margin>
The **Egyptians** were named after a certain king of theirs called **Aegyptus**. Previously, they were called **Aereans**. In the Hebrew language, however, "Egyptians" is interpreted as "those who afflict," because they afflicted God’s people until they were liberated by divine help. The **Armenians** are named after **Armenus**, one of the leaders of Jason <note>the leader of the Argonauts</note>; after Jason was lost and the multitude was wandering aimlessly, Armenus gathered them and founded Armenia, giving the nation a name from his own vocabulary. There is a boundary there which divides them from the **Scythians**, known as **Scythia**, from which boundary some say the **Scythians** are named. They have always been considered a very ancient race. They founded the kingdoms of the **Parthians** and the **Bactrians**. Their women founded the kingdoms of the **Amazons**. The **Massagetae** are of Scythian origin. They are called Massagetae as if to say "heavy" <note>original: "graves"</note>, meaning "strong Getae." For in this way, the historian Livy speaks of "heavy silver," meaning silver in masses. These are the people who live in the northern ridges between the Scythians and the **Albanians**. The **Amazons** were so named either because they lived together without men, as if *amacos* <note>meaning "without husbands"</note>, or because they had their right breasts burnt away so that the shooting of arrows would not be hindered, as if *aneu mazou* <note>original: "ανευ μαζου," Greek for "without breast"</note>. Indeed, they used to expose the side where the breast had been burnt. Justin <note>the Roman historian</note> calls them "one-breasted" <note>original: "unimamas"</note>. For this is what *Amazon* means: as if *anc lmacoin*, that is, "without breast." These women no longer exist; their nations were destroyed unto extinction partly by Hercules, partly by Achilles, or by Alexander.

<margin>Albanians, who are born more [white]; they see better at night than by day</margin>
In the regions of Asiatic Scythia, there are nations who believe themselves to be descendants of Jason; they are born with white hair <note>original: "albo crine"</note> due to the constant snows. This very color of the hair gave the nation its name, and thus they are called **Albanians**. Their eyes have a bluish-gray <note>original: "glauca"</note> pupil—that is, a variegated one—so much so that they see better at night than by day. The Albanians were neighbors to the Amazons. Those formerly called **Huns** were later named **Avars** after their own king. They first lived in the farthest reaches of Maeotis, between the icy Tanais <note>the Don River</note> and the fierce peoples of the Massagetae.

<column-break/>

Then, on swift horses, they broke through the rugged cliffs of the Caucasus where Alexander’s gates had confined the wild nations, and they held the East captive for twenty years, demanding an annual tribute from the Egyptians and Ethiopians. The race of the **Trojans** was previously called **Dardanian**, named after King **Dardanus**. For Dardanus and **Iasius** were brothers who set out from Greece; Iasius reached Thrace, and Dardanus reached Phrygia, where he was the first to reign. After him came his son **Erichthonius**, then his grandson **Tros**, from whom the Trojans are named. The **Galatians** are known to be **Gauls**; they were summoned by the king of Bithynia for military aid and, after achieving victory, they divided the kingdom with him. Thus, having been mixed with the Greeks, they were first called **Gallogreci**, but now they are called **Galatians** after the ancient name of the Gauls. The **Greeks** were first called **Thessalians** after **Thessalus**, and later called Greeks after King **Graecus**. Properly speaking, the Greeks were called Thessalians. It is said that the **Lapiths** were a nation of Thessaly living long ago around the river Peneus, named after **Lapitha**, the daughter of Apollo. The **Sicyonians** are Greeks named after King **Sicyon**. They were first called **Aegialeans** after King **Aegialeus**, who first ruled the Sicyonians and after whom the city of **Aegialea** was named (which is now called the **Peloponnese** after its king, **Pelops**). These are also the **Arcadians**, named after King **Arcas**, the son of Jupiter and Callisto. The **Danaans** are named after King **Danaus**. They are also called **Argives** after their founder, **Argus**. After **Apis**, the king of the Greeks, died, his son Argus succeeded to the kingdom, and from him they were called Argives; after his death, they even began to regard him as a god, honored with a temple and sacrifice. The **Achaeans**, who are also the **Achaeans** <note>original: "Achiui"</note>, are named after **Achaeus**, the son of Jupiter. The **Pelasgians** are so named because they seemed to arrive in Italy like birds with spreading sails in the springtime. For Varro records that they were the first to land in Italy. The Greeks, however, claim the Pelasgians were named after **Pelasgus**, the son of Jupiter and Larissa. The **Myrmidones** were the companions of Achilles, and the **Dolopes** the companions of Pyrrhus. They were called Myrmidons because of their cunning, as if they were *myrmices* <note>Greek: μύρμηκες</note>, that is, "ants." Eratosthenes, however, says the Myrmidons were named after their leader **Myrmidon**, the son of Jupiter and Eurymedusa. **Agranos** succeeded **Cecrops** as king of the Athenians; his daughter, named **Atthis**, gave her name to both the region and the people. From her, they were called **Attics**, who are the **Athenians**. **Ion**, a brave man, called these same Athenians **Ionians** after his own name. The **Macedonians** were previously called **Emathians** from the name of King **Emathion**; later they were called Macedonians from King **Macedon**, the maternal grandson of Deucalion. The **Epirotes** were first called **Pyrrhidae** from **Pyrrhus**, the son of Achilles; later, under King Pyrrhus, they presumed to cross over into Italy. **Dorus** was the son of Neptune and Ellepis, from whom the **Dorians** derive their origin and name. They are a part of the Greek nation, from whom the third dialect of the Greeks is named, which is called **Doric**. The **Lacedaemonians** <note>Spartans</note> are named after **Lacedaemon**, the son of Semele and Jupiter. These people, persevering for a long time in war and fearing the **Messenians**, were afraid that they would lose the hope of offspring due to the length of the conflict. They ordered that their virgins should sleep with the young men who had been left at home; and thus from...

# Book IX

...through the promiscuous cohabitation of virgins and husbands, youths were born of uncertain parentage and were called **Spartans** because of the mark of maternal shame <note>The author suggests the name comes from 'spurius' or 'scattered' origins</note>. For they are the same people as the **Lacedaemonians**. They are called Spartans as if "drawn together" <note>original: *contractos*</note> because of their sudden arrival against Cadmus, having flocked together from every direction. The **Thracians** are recorded as being descended from and named after the son of Japheth who was called Tiras, as was said previously. Although the pagans claim they were named from their customs because they are savage <note>original: *truces*</note>. Indeed, they were the most savage of all nations. Hence many fables are remembered about them: that they sacrificed captives to their gods and were accustomed to drink human blood from the bones of skulls. Of these, **Virgil** says: "Alas, flee the cruel lands, flee the greedy shore," <note>Aeneid 3.44</note> as if speaking of a cruel and greedy people. The **Histrian** race <note>original: *Istroitũ*, referring to the Istrians</note> derives its origin from the Colchians who, sent to pursue the Argonauts, entered the river Ister from the Black Sea; they were named after the name of the river from which they had retreated from the sea. The **Romans** were named after the name of **Romulus**, who founded the city of Rome and gave his name to the people and the city. Before that, they were called Saturnians after Saturn, and Latins after Latinus. For **Latinus** was a king of Italy who called the Latins by his own name; they were later called Romans. They were also called **Quirites** because Romulus was called Quirinus, as he always used a spear, which in the language of the Sabines is called a *quiris*. **Italus**, **Sabinus**, and **Sicanus** were brothers, from whom names were given to the people themselves and their regions. For from Italus came the **Italians**, from Sabinus the **Sabines**, 
<margin>Sicilians</margin>
and from Sicanus the **Sicanians**, who were also surnamed **Sicilians**. They are also called Sicilienses. The **Tuscans** are a people of Italy, named from the frequency of their sacrifices and incense <note>original: *thuris*</note>; that is, from the Greek *apo tou thuein* <note>original: απο του θυειν, meaning "from sacrificing"</note>. The **Umbrians** are a people of Italy, but are the offspring of the ancient Gauls who inhabit the Apennine mountains. History records that they survived the rains <note>original: *imbribus*</note> during a time of watery disaster, and for this reason were named Umbrians in Greek. The **Marsians** are a people of Italy named after Marsyas, a companion of Father Liber <note>another name for Bacchus/Dionysus</note>, who showed them the use of vines; because of this they made a statue for him, which the Romans took away after the Marsians were defeated. The Greeks, however, call the Marsians *ruscos*, or as it were *ophiouchous* <note>original: οφιουχους, meaning "snake-handlers"</note>, because they have many serpents <note>original: οφις, *ophis*, meaning "serpent"</note> and are harmless to them through the spells of their songs. They inhabit the region of the Apennine mountains along with the Umbrians. The **Goths** are thought to be named after Magog, the son of Japheth, from the similarity of the last syllable. The ancients called them *Getae* rather than Goths—a brave and most powerful race, tall in stature and terrifying in their type of armor. Of them **Lucan** says: "Let the Dacian press from here, from there let the Gete meet the Iberians." <note>Pharsalia 2.54</note> The **Dacians**, however, were the offspring of the Goths, and it is thought they were called Dacians as if *Dagos*, because they were created from the stock of the Goths. Of them it is said: "You will go far as wanderers to the cold north." The **Bessi** were barbarians who are believed to be so named from a multitude of oxen <note>original: *boum*</note>. Of them someone said: "He who inhabits the middle of the earth, or that capped dweller of the bank with many oxen." The **Bipedes** used foot-combat <note>original: *pedestri praelio*</note> rather than cavalry, and for this reason they were so named. The **Sarmatians** used to ride armed through the open plains before Lentulus

<column-break/>

prevented them from crossing the Danube; and from then on they are thought to have been named Sarmatians because of their "zeal for arms" <note>original: *studium armorum*</note>. The river **Ianus** is said to be beyond the Danube, from which the **Alani** are named; just as the people living near Lake **Lemannus** <note>Lake Geneva</note> are called **Alamanni**. Of them Lucan says: "They deserted the tents fixed by hollow Lemanus." <note>Pharsalia 1.396</note> The **Longobards** <note>Lombards</note> are commonly said 
<margin>long-bearded</margin>
to be named from their long and never-shorn beards. The **Vandals** 
<margin>Vandals</margin>
are said to have lived near and taken their name from the river **Vandalius**, which breaks out from the farthest parts of Gaul. The tribes of **Germany** are so named because 
<margin>Germans</margin>
they have "immense bodies" <note>original: *immania corpora*</note> and are immense nations, hardened by the most severe cold. They derived these customs from the very chill of the climate: fierce in spirit and always untamed, living by plunder and hunting. There are many tribes among them, varying in arms, differing in dress, clashing in languages, and uncertain in the origin of their names, such as the Tolcrates, Famsivari, Quadi, Tungri, Marcomanni, Bruteri, Chamavi, Blangiani, and Tubantes; whose immensity and barbarity signify a certain horror even in their very names. The **Suebi** were a part of the Germans at the northern 
<margin>Suebi</margin>
edge, of whom Lucan says: "From the far north he pours forth the blond Suebi." <note>Pharsalia 2.51</note> Many have handed down that there were a hundred districts and peoples of them. The Suebi are thought to be named from Mount **Suevus**, which marks the beginning of Germany in the east. The **Burgundians** once inhabited these places; having been subdued by the Romans in inner Germany and positioned along the borders of the camps by Tiberius Caesar, they grew into a great nation and thus took their name from the places. For the frequent dwellings established along the borders are commonly called *burgi* <note>fortified towns</note>. These people later became rebels against the Romans, and more than eighty thousand armed men settled on the banks of the Rhine and kept the name of the nation. The race of the **Saxons**, situated on the shores 
<margin>Saxons</margin>
and impassable marshes of the Ocean, is capable in virtue and agility. Whence they are named because they are a "hard and most strong" <note>original: *saxum*, meaning rock/stone</note> race of men, surpassing others in piracy. The 
<margin>Franks</margin>
**Franks** are thought to be named after a certain leader of their own. Others believe they were named from the "ferocity" <note>original: *feritate*</note> of their customs. For there are in them unrefined customs and a natural ferocity of spirit. Some suspect the 
<margin>Britons</margin>
**Britons** were named in Latin because they are "dull" <note>original: *bruti*</note>. They are a race within the Ocean, with the sea poured between, positioned as if outside the world; of whom **Virgil** says: "The Britons, divided from the whole world." <note>Eclogues 1.66</note> The 
<margin>Scots</margin>
**Scots**, in their own language, have a name from their "painted body" <note>referring to tattoos</note>, because they are marked with iron needles and ink with the sting of various figures. The **Gauls** 
<margin>Gauls</margin>
were named from the "whiteness" <note>original: *candore*</note> of their bodies. For *gala* in Greek means "milk" <note>original: γαλα</note>. Whence Virgil also calls them thus when he says of them: "Then their milky necks are entwined with gold." <note>Aeneid 8.660</note> For according to the diversity of the climate, the faces of men, their colors, the sizes of their bodies, and the diversities of their spirits exist. Hence we see that the Romans are grave, the Greeks are light, the Africans are shifty, and the Gauls are naturally fierce and of a sharper disposition, which the nature of the climates produces. <meta>This page continues the catalog of nations from Book IX of the Etymologies, shifting focus to the tribes of the Iberian Peninsula (Spain), the various peoples of Africa, and legendary groups like the Titans and the Antipodes.</meta>

...surnamed the **Vaccaei**, of whom it is believed the poet spoke: "The Vaccaei wandering in concealment" <note>original: *Latenteque vagantes vaccei*</note>. These people dwell on the ridges of the Pyrenees throughout the vast solitude of the mountains. They are also called the **Vascones** <note>The ancestors of the modern Basques</note>, as if "Vaccones," with the letter *c* changed into *s*. After Gnaeus Pompey had subdued Spain and was hurrying to his triumph, he brought them down from the ridges of the Pyrenees and gathered them into one town. From this, the city received the name "City of the Gathered" <note>original: *conuenarum urbs*, referring to Lugdunum Convenarum</note>. The **Spaniards** were first called **Iberians** after the river Hiberus <note>The Ebro</note>; later they were surnamed Spaniards from Hispalis <note>Seville</note>. The **Galicians** <note>original: *Gallici*</note> are named for their whiteness <note>original: *candore*</note>, hence they are also called "Galli" <note>Gauls</note>, for they are whiter than the rest of the peoples of Spain. They claim a Greek origin for themselves, which is why they are naturally clever in talent. For it is said that after the end of the Trojan War, **Teucer**—having become hated by his father Telamon due to the death of his brother Ajax—was not received into the kingdom and went to Cyprus. There he founded a city named Salamis after his ancient homeland; from there he set out for Gallaecia, and after establishing settlements, he gave the name to the nation from that place. The **Asturians**, a people of Spain, are so called because they dwell around the river Astura, hemmed in by mountains and thick forests. The **Cantabrians**, a people of Spain, are named from the word for a city and the river Hiberus, upon which they are situated. Their spirit is inclined more toward banditry than toward warfare, and they are always ready to endure lashes. The **Celtiberians** were descended from the Celtic Gauls, from whose name the region of Celtiberia was called. For from the Spanish river Hiberus, where they settled, and from the Gauls who were called Celts, the name **Celtiberi** was coined by mixing both terms. The **Africans** were named after one of the descendants of Abraham who was called **Afer**, who is said to have led an army against Libya and settled there after defeating his enemies; his descendants called both the people "Afri" and the land "Africa" from the name of their ancestor. The **Punics** <note>original: *Peni*</note>, however, are the Carthaginians, named after the Phoenicians who set out with Dido. The **Tyrians** are named after the Phoenician city of Tyre, from which they set out and came to the coast of Africa. The **Getulians** <note>original: *Getuli*</note> are said by the Greeks to have been people who, boarding ships in a great multitude from their own lands, occupied the regions of the Syrtes in Libya; and because they had come from the Getae <note>Goths</note>, they were surnamed Getulians by a derivation of the name. From this, there is an opinion among the **Goths** that, because of an ancient kinship, they call the **Moors** their relatives by blood. At the beginning, the **Libyans** held Africa, then the Africans, after that the Getulians, and finally the **Moors** and the **Numidians**. The Moors and Numidians, as the Africans believe, took both their origin and their name in this way: after **Hercules** died in Spain, his army—composed of various nations—sought settlements for themselves here and there once their leader was lost. From that number, the **Medes**, **Persians**, and **Armenians** were carried across to Africa by ships and occupied the first places by the sea. But because the Persians could not find material in the fields for building houses, and their unknown language prohibited trade, they wandered through the open fields and various solitudes. From this wandering for pasture <note>original: *pabulationibus vagabundis*</note>, they called themselves **Numidians** in their own language—that is, "wanderers and erring ones without a town" <note>Isidore links "Numidian" to the Greek *nomados* (nomad)</note>. The Medes, however, mixed with the Libyans who first inhabited Spain; the Libyans gradually corrupted their name in their barbarian tongue, calling the Medes "**Moors**" <note>original: *Mauros*</note>, although the Moors were so named by the Greeks because of their color. The Greeks...
<meta>catchword: The Greeks</meta>

<column-break/>

...for the Greeks call black *mauron*. Indeed, being blasted by the heat, they take on the appearance of a dark color. **Massylia** is a city of Africa not far from Mount Atlas and the Gardens of the Hesperides, from which city the **Massylians** are named, whom we corruptly call the **Massulians**. Of them, **Virgil** says: "From here the priestess of the Massylian race was shown to me." <note>Aeneid 4.483</note> The **Gaulalum** are nations fighting from the south all the way to the western ocean. The island of Gauloen gave them their name; it is near Ethiopia, where no serpent is born nor can live. The **Garamantes** are a people of Africa dwelling near Cyrene, named after King **Garamas**, the son of Apollo, who founded the town of Garama there after his own name. They are the first among the nations of the **Ethiopians**, of whom Virgil says: "The furthest Garamantes." <note>Eclogues 8.44</note> They are called "furthest" because they are savage and removed from human fellowship. The **Hesperians** are those who dwell around Spain, for Spain is called **Hesperia** <note>The Land of the West</note>. The **Ethiopians** are named after the son of Ham who was called **Cush**, from whom they draw their origin. For in the Hebrew language, *Cush* is interpreted as "Ethiopian" <note>original: *ethiops*</note>. These people once arose from the river Indus and settled near Egypt between the Nile and the Ocean in the south, under the very proximity of the sun. There are three groups of them: the Hesperians, the Garamantes, and the Indians. The Hesperians are of the west, the Garamantes of Tripoli, and the Indians of the east. The **Troglodytes** <note>original: *Trogodite*</note>, a nation of Ethiopians, are so named because they excel in such speed that they can catch wild beasts by running on foot. The **Panphagi** <note>original: *Panphagi*, meaning 'all-eaters'</note> are in Ethiopia; their food is whatever can be chewed, and they eat all things produced by chance, whence they are named. The **Ichthyophagi** <note>meaning 'fish-eaters'</note> are those who excel at hunting in the sea and are nourished only by fish. These hold the mountainous regions beyond the Indians; **Alexander the Great**, having subdued them, forbade them from eating fish. The **Anthropophagi** <note>meaning 'man-eaters'</note> are a very harsh nation situated below the region of the Syrtes; because they feed on human flesh, they are named Anthropophagi. And so, just as with these, the names of other nations have been changed through the ages either by kings, or places, or customs, or any other causes, so that the original root of their name is not evident due to the antiquity of those times. Now, as for those called the **Antipodes**, because they are thought to be opposite our footprints, as if placed under the earth they tread with feet turned against ours—there is no reason to believe this. Neither the solidity [of the earth] nor the center of the earth allows it, nor does any historical knowledge confirm it; rather, poets guess this by a kind of reasoning. It is said there were certain **Titans** in Greece, men of robust and excellent strength; the fables say they were created by the Earth, who was angry at the gods, for her revenge. Whence they were called Titans <insert>...that is, from 'vengeance' as if</insert> they existed as armed men against the gods for the sake of avenging their mother Earth. The fables feign that they were defeated and destroyed by Jove in war, because of which they perished from lightning bolts cast from heaven.

### Chapter III. On kingdoms and military terms.

"Kingdom" <note>original: *Regnum*</note> is named from "Kings" <note>original: *regibus*</note>. For just as kings are named from "ruling" <note>original: *regendo*</note>, so the kingdom is named from kings. Every nation has held a kingdom in its own time, such as the **Assyrians**, **Medes**, **Persians**, **Egyptians**, **Greeks**, or **Romans**, whose successions the lot of time has thus rotated...

<summary>This page explores the etymological origins of various ethnic groups in Spain and Africa, including the Basques, Galicians, and Ethiopians, while also dismissing the existence of the Antipodes and defining the concept of a kingdom.</summary>

<meta>This page continues Book IX of the Etymologies, moving from the description of nations and tribes to the origins of political titles and military ranks. It explores how the names of rulers and soldiers reflect their duties and historical beginnings.</meta>

# IX

...one would dissolve from the other. Among all the kingdoms of the earth, two kingdoms are said to be more glorious than the others: first that of the **Assyrians**, then that of the **Romans**, so that they are ordered and distinguished between themselves by times and places. For just as the former was earlier and the latter later, so the former arose in the East and the latter in the West. Finally, at the end of the one, the beginning of the other followed immediately. Other kingdoms and other kings are considered as if they were appendages to these two.

**Kings** <note>original: *Reges*</note> are named from "ruling" <note>original: *regendo*</note>; for just as a priest is named from "sanctifying," so a king is named from ruling. But he does not rule who does not correct. Therefore, by doing right <note>original: *recte faciendo*</note>, he holds the name of king; by sinning, he loses it. Hence among the ancients there was such a proverb: "You will be king if you do right; if you do not, you will not be." The primary virtues of a king are two: **justice** and **piety**. However, piety is praised more in kings, for justice by itself is severe.

**Consuls** are named from "consulting" <note>original: *consulendo*</note>, just as kings are from ruling and laws <note>original: *leges*</note> from "reading" <note>original: *legendo*</note>. For when the Romans could no longer bear the proud domination of kings, they established for themselves annual commands and two consuls. For the pride of a king was not the benevolence of one consulting, but the arrogance of one dominating. From this, therefore, they were called "consuls," either from consulting the citizens or from ruling everything by counsel. They chose to change these men every single year so that no one would remain insolent for long, and so that moderation might quickly come to the rescue. There were two of them as equals because one managed civil affairs and the other managed military affairs. They reigned for four hundred and sixty-seven years.

**Proconsuls** were subject to the consuls; they were called proconsuls because they performed the role of a consul <note>original: *vice consulis*</note>, just as a procurator performs the role of a curator (that is, an agent). **Ex-consuls** are so named because they have already exited the consulship or have stepped down after their year of service was completed.

**Dictators** were created by the Romans in the fifth year after the kings were expelled, when the son-in-law of Tarquin had gathered a massive army against Rome to avenge the injury to his father-in-law. These men exercised command for a five-year period. They were greater in honor than the consuls, who held power for only one year. They were called "dictators" as if they were "leaders" and "instructors" <note>original: *praeceptores*</note>. Hence they were also called "masters of the people," and from this, "edicts" are named.

The name of the **Caesars** began with **Julius**, who, after stirring up civil war, was the first of the Romans to obtain sole leadership. He was called "Caesar" because he was brought out and led forth from his dead mother's womb having been cut <note>original: *caeso*</note>, or because he was born with a full head of hair <note>original: *caesarie*</note>. From him, subsequent emperors were called "Caesars" because they were hairy. For those who were removed from a cut womb were called *caesones* and *caesares*. He was called **Julius** because he drew his origin from Iulus, the son of Aeneas, as **Virgil** confirms: "Julius, a name descended from the great Iulus."

The title **Emperor** <note>original: *Imperator*</note> among the Romans was originally only used by those who held the highest military command; thus they were called "emperors" from "commanding" <note>original: *imperando*</note> the army. But while leaders long used the titles of emperors, the Senate decreed that this should be the specific name of **Augustus Caesar**, so that he might be distinguished from the other kings of nations; subsequent Caesars have usurped this title up to the present. For it is common for the name of the first king to be held by those who follow, just as among the Albans all kings were called "Silvii" from the name of Silvius, and so among the Persians they were called "Arsacidae," and among the Egy-

<column-break/>

ptians "Ptolemies," and among the Athenians "Cecropidae."

**Augustus** is therefore a name of empire among the Romans, because they once "increased" <note>original: *augerent*</note> the republic by enlarging it. The Senate first gave this name to **Octavian Caesar** so that, because he had increased the lands, he might be consecrated by that very name and title. While this same Octavian was called both Caesar and Emperor as well as Augustus, later, while he was waiting for the games and it was shouted to him by the people that he should also be called "Lord" <note>original: *dominus*</note>, he immediately repressed such unseemly flatteries with his hand and a turned face. As a man, he declined the title of Lord, and on the following day he rebuked the whole city with a very serious edict; after this, he did not permit himself to be called "Lord" even by his own children. He was the son of Atia, who was born from the sister of Julius Caesar.

Kings are called **basileis** among the Greeks for this reason: because they support the people just as "bases" <note>original: *bases*</note> support a structure. Hence also the bases of columns have "crowns." For the more someone is placed in charge, the more he is weighed down by the burden of labor.

**Tyrants** <note>original: *Tyranni*</note> is a Greek term; in Latin, the same word means "kings." For among the ancients, there was no distinction between a king and a tyrant, as in: "It was part of my peace to have touched the tyrant's right hand." For strong kings were called tyrants. For *tyro* means "strong," of whom the Lord speaks, saying: "Through me kings reign, and through me tyrants hold the earth." Only later did it happen in common usage that the most wicked and dishonest kings were called "tyrants"—those who exercise a desire for luxurious domination and a most cruel mastery over the people.

**Prince** <note>original: *Princeps*</note> signifies a position of both dignity and rank, as in that line of Virgil: "Prince Turnus threw the burning torch," meaning "the first." Or "prince" is named from the meaning of "taking" <note>original: *capiendi*</note>, because he takes the first place, just as a "burgess" <note>original: *municeps*</note> is named from the one who takes up duties <note>original: *munia*</note>.

A **Leader** <note>original: *Dux*</note> is so called because he is the conductor of an army. However, not everyone who is a "prince" or a "leader" can also be called a "king." In war, it is more fitting to name a man a "leader" than a "king." For this name expresses the one leading in battle. Hence Virgil says: "Of the leader Evander." And **Sallust**: "The more eagerly each good man presented himself in the sight of the leader." He did not say "in the sight of the consul."

**Monarchs** are those who hold sole leadership, such as **Alexander** was among the Greeks and Julius was among the Romans. Hence it is called a "**monarchy**." For *monos* is the Greek name for "singularity," and *archia* is "leadership."

**Tetrarchs** are those who hold a fourth part of a kingdom. For *tetra* is "four," such as **Philip** was in Judea.

**Patricians** are so called for this reason: that just as fathers <note>original: *patres*</note> provide for their children, so they provide for the republic.

**Prefects** are named because they are "placed in charge" <note>original: *praesint*</note> of the praetorium. **Praetors** are the same as prefects, as if they were "those placed before." **Presidents** <note>original: *Praesides*</note> are so named because they hold the "guardianship" <note>original: *tutela*</note> of a certain place. **Tribunes** are named because they "attribute" <note>original: *tribuunt*</note> rights to the soldiers or the common people.

**Chiliarchs** are those who are in charge of a thousand <note>Greek *chilioi*</note> soldiers, whom we call "millenarians"; this is a Greek name. **Centurions** are so called because they are in charge of a hundred <note>Latin *centum*</note> soldiers, just as "fifty-men" are at the head of fifty soldiers, and **decans** are named from being placed over ten soldiers.

A **Soldier** <note>original: *Miles*</note> is so named because there were originally a thousand <note>original: *mille*</note> in one unit, or because one is chosen from a thousand. **Romulus** first selected soldiers from his own people and gave them this name. **Liber** <note>The god Bacchus/Dionysus</note> first taught the order of military service. A soldier is called either "ordinary" or "extraordinary." An **ordinary** soldier is one who serves according to the rank and has not yet...

<summary>This page explains the etymological origins of various political and military titles, linking Roman and Greek terminology to Latin roots to define the roles and virtues of rulers and soldiers.</summary>
<keywords>kingship, consuls, Caesar, Augustus, tyrants, military ranks, etymology, Roman history, political theory, Isidore of Seville</keywords>

--- Page 104 ---
<meta>This page continues Isidore of Seville's ninth book of the Etymologies, specifically moving through the hierarchy and terminology of the Roman military and concluding with the definition of a citizen and a household.</meta>

...attained some rank of honor. For he is a **common soldier** <note>original: "gregarius"</note>, that is, of the humble ranks of service. **Extraordinary soldiers** <note>original: "extraordinarii"</note> are those who are promoted out of their regular order on account of their valor. **Veterans** <note>original: "emeriti"</note> are those released from military service who are no longer in the habit of battle; they are so called because they have "earned" <note>original: "mereri"</note> their rest, specifically from the stipends they earned. They are also called veterans because they are no longer in active use for battle, but after many labors of service, they attain the right to rest. **Cavalrymen** <note>original: "equestres"</note> are named from sitting upon a horse <note>original: "equo"</note>. Likewise, such a person serves in the equestrian order. **Recruits** <note>original: "tyrones"</note> are called the strong young men who are assigned to service and are considered capable of bearing arms. These are judged not only by their birth but by their appearance and physical health. Thus they are called "recruits," and they are not soldiers until they have been approved by the military oath. It was the Roman military custom for youths to first be trained in arms. Indeed, at sixteen years of age, recruits began their service, at which age they also lived under guardians; of whom **Virgil** <note>Publius Virgilius Maro, the Roman epic poet</note> says: "And youth in its first flower." It is well known that **slaves** never served, unless they were first freed from servitude—except in the time of **Hannibal**, when after the Battle of Cannae the Romans were in such necessity that they did not even have the opportunity to free the slaves. **Deserters** <note>original: "desertores"</note> are named because they wander after deserting their military duties. These are forbidden from giving their names to other units; but if they have not committed a major offense, they are restored to their original units. However, those who desert the army to go over to the enemy are also called deserters. **Conscripted** <note>original: "conscripti"</note> soldiers are so named because they are enrolled <note>original: "conseruntur"</note> in the records by the one who is to lead them; just as **transferred** <note>original: "transcripti"</note> soldiers are called when they pass from one legion to another. **Adjutants** <note>original: "optiones"</note> are named because they are "chosen" <note>original: "electi"</note>; for "to choose" <note>original: "optare"</note> means to select, as in the phrase: "He chose a place for his kingdom," meaning he selected it. **Sentinels** <note>original: "excubitores"</note> are so called because they always keep watch <note>original: "excubias"</note>. For they are from the number of soldiers and they keep watch at the gates for the royal guard. "Excubiae" are for the day, and "vigils" <note>original: "vigiliae"</note> are for the night; hence also "watchmen" <note>original: "vigiles"</note>. The **skirmishers** <note>original: "velites"</note> were a type of soldier among the Romans, named from "flying about" <note>original: "volitando"</note>. For agile youths were selected to sit behind the backs of the horsemen with their arms, and as soon as they reached the enemy, they leaped down from the horses. Immediately acting as infantry on one side, while the horsemen who carried them fought on the other, they threw the enemy into confusion. By these skirmishers, Hannibal’s **elephants** were once driven back when they could no longer be ruled by their handlers; they were killed by driving a carpenter's chisel between their ears. **Camps** <note>original: "castra"</note> are where soldiers stay. They are called *castra* as if they were "chaste" <note>original: "casta"</note>, because there lust would be "castrated" <note>original: "castraretur"</note>. For no woman was ever present among them. **Military service** <note>original: "militia"</note> is named from "soldiers" <note>original: "militibus"</note>, or from "many" <note>original: "multis"</note> as if it were a "business of many" <note>original: "multiria"</note>, or from the "mass" <note>original: "mole"</note> of things, as if a "massive task" <note>original: "moleatia"</note>. A **legion** <note>original: "legio"</note> consists of six thousand armed men, named from being "selected" <note>original: "electo" (chosen)</note>, as if chosen for arms. Properly speaking, it is called a *phalanx* in the language of the Macedonians, a *caterva* by the Gauls, and a "legion" by us. A legion has sixty **centuries**, thirty **maniples**, twelve **cohorts**, two hundred **troops**, and fifteen **choirs**. A century is a part of the army divided into one hundred soldiers. Hence also those who lead them are called

<column-break/>

**centurions**. **Substitutes** <note>original: "succenturiati"</note> are not those in the first century but those in the second, as if "under the first century" <note>original: "sub prima centuria"</note>; they are also arranged and placed at lookout points in war so that if the first unit fails, these whom we said were "under" them might aid the laboring first unit. Hence an ambusher is also called "substituted," as if prepared with deceitful arms. A **maniple** <note>original: "manipulus"</note> is a leadership of soldiers. They are called maniples either because they first began battle by hand <note>original: "manu"</note>, or because before there were standards, they made for themselves "handfuls" <note>original: "manipulos"</note>—that is, bundles of straw or some herb—to serve as signals; from which signal the soldiers were nicknamed "maniplares." Of whom **Lucan** <note>Marcus Annaeus Lucanus, a Roman poet</note> says: "The maniple immediately calls the armed men to the standards." A **troop** <note>original: "turma"</note> consists of thirty horsemen. For the Roman horsemen in one tribe were three hundred; ten were given from each of the centuries to make a troop. A **cohort** <note>original: "cohors"</note> has five hundred soldiers. There are three types of military service: the **oath** <note>original: "sacramentum"</note>, the **summons** <note>original: "evocatio"</note>, and the **emergency levy** <note>original: "coniuratio"</note>. The oath is when, after selection, each soldier swears not to depart from service except after his stipends—that is, his time of service—are completed; and these are those who have full service, for they are held for twenty-five years. A summons is when, for a sudden war, not only soldiers but all others are called out. From this the consul was also accustomed to say: "Let him who wants the Republic to be safe follow me." An emergency levy is what happens in a riot <note>original: "tumultu"</note> when a danger near the city does not allow for each man to swear individually, but a multitude is suddenly gathered and fanned into a "tumultuous" anger. This is also called a "tumultuation." In a battle line, there are these forms: the **army**, the **fleet**, the **knot**, the **wedge**, the **wings**, the **horns**, and the **column**; which borrow their forms and names from the very things from which they are transferred. A **battle line** <note>original: "acies"</note> is so called because it is armed with iron and the "sharpness" <note>original: "acumine"</note> of swords. An **army** <note>original: "exercitus"</note> is a multitude of one kind, named from "exercise" <note>original: "exercitatione"</note> in war. **Fleets** <note>original: "classes"</note> were named because of the division of the army, which were later called maniples; hence **Virgil** says: "Here is the place for the fleets, here the lines were accustomed to clash." For later it was also applied to fleets of ships. A **knot** <note>original: "nodus"</note> is properly a dense multitude of infantry, just as a "troop" is of cavalry. It is called a knot because of the difficulty with which a man can be disentangled from it. A **wedge** <note>original: "cuneus"</note> is a multitude of soldiers collected into one. Hence, because they come together into one, the very act of coming together into one is named a "wedge" as if "co-united" <note>original: "couneus"</note>, because they are all driven into one. **Wings** <note>original: "alae"</note> in an army are said to be thirty horsemen. Horsemen are called wings for this reason: because they cover the infantry in the manner of wings. **Horns** <note>original: "cornua" (corners)</note> are the extremities of an army, because they are curved. It is called a **column** <note>original: "agmen"</note> when the army makes a journey, named from "doing" <note>original: "agendo"</note>, that is, going. **Plautus** <note>Titus Maccius Plautus, a Roman playwright</note> says: "Where are you taking yourself?" <note>original: "Quo te agis"</note>. For it is a walking army. It is called a column because it is directed in length, as is usual when an army proceeds through gates; anything else is so called by an abuse of the term.

->Chapter 4: On Citizens<-

The names of commands and military terms have been partially discussed; next, let us briefly add the names of citizens. **Citizens** <note>original: "ciues"</note> are so called because they live "coming together" <note>original: "coeuntes"</note> into one, so that life might be common, organized, and protected. A **house** <note>original: "domus"</note> is the dwelling of a single family.
